Oily skin doesn't need moisturiser? Myth. 💧
Skipping it can dehydrate your skin, and dehydrated skin can make even more oil. A light gel moisturiser fixes it.

Should you tip in Korea? Myth. 💸
Tipping isn't part of the culture, in restaurants or taxis, and it can even confuse staff. Pay the bill and say 감사합니다.

여기요! (yeo-gi-yo) = over here! Calling out is normal and polite. If there's a bell on the table, press it instead.

Hot water opens your pores? Myth. 🚿
Pores have no muscles, so they can't open or close. Heat only softens the oil inside, and very hot water dries your skin out. Lukewarm, every time.

Which floor number do Korean elevators often hide? 🛗
The 4th. 사 (four) sounds like the word for death, so many buildings show F instead of 4.

Korean convenience stores only sell snacks? Myth. 🏪
They sell hot meals, top up your T-money card, and most have an ATM. Many never close. Lost, hungry or out of cash? Find a 편의점.

What hyaluronic acid actually does to dry skin 💧
It's a humectant: it pulls water into the top layer of your skin and holds it there, so skin looks plumper. Apply on damp skin, then seal with a moisturiser.
On the label: sodium hyaluronate, hyaluronic acid.

보습 (bo-seup) means moisturising: it helps your skin hold on to water. Usually with ceramides, glycerin or hyaluronic acid.

Natural means gentle? Myth. 🌿
Fragrant plant oils and extracts are some of the most common skin irritants. Poison ivy is natural too. Judge the ingredient, not the word on the front.

What does PA++++ mean on a Korean sunscreen? ☀️
It's the UVA rating. SPF mostly measures UVB, the burning rays. PA rates UVA, the ones that age your skin. ++++ is the highest grade.
